story: A.A. Bondy was the frontman of the Alabama band Verbena before he went solo, with American Hearts in 2007, When the Devil's Loose in 2009 and Believers in 2011. Believers came out on Fat Possum on September 13, 2011, recorded in Los Angeles with Rob Schnapf, and is his most band-oriented album; the A.V. Club liked it. He played Pickathon in 2012, then stepped away for several years and returned with Enderness in 2019.
artist_reel_line: Enderness came in 2019 after years away.

intro: A psych-folk songwriter, here for the fourth time.
story: Alela Diane was born on April 20, 1983, in Nevada City, California, and Joanna Newsom, from the same town, invited her to play her first solo shows. She moved to Portland after recording The Pirate's Gospel so she wouldn't vanish into the woodwork of Nevada City, she told Westword. That album was self-released in 2004 and reissued by Holocene in 2006 and in the UK in 2007, with praise in The Times and NME; To Be Still, on Rough Trade in 2009, landed in France's top 20. Alela Diane & Wild Divine, made with her father Tom Menig, came in 2011. She played Pickathon in 2007, 2009, 2011 and 2012, and Who's Keeping Time? came out on Loose in 2026.

intro: Erika Wennerstrom's powerhouse band, back after 2010.
story: Heartless Bastards formed in Cincinnati in 2003 as a recording project of Erika Wennerstrom, and moved to Austin in 2007. The Mountain came out on Fat Possum in 2009, and Arrow, their fourth album, on February 14, 2012, the year of their second Pickathon. They returned in 2015, and A Beautiful Life came out in 2021.
artist_reel_line: Arrow, their fourth album, came out on February 14, 2012.

intro: A heart-on-sleeve songwriter, here for the fourth time.
story: Sean Scolnick took the stage name Langhorne Slim from his hometown of Langhorne, Pennsylvania. Be Set Free came out on Kemado on September 29, 2009, recorded in Portland and produced by the Decemberists' Chris Funk, with Tucker Martine mixing, and NPR's World Cafe called him savvy, a true professional with the excitement of a newcomer. He played Pickathon in 2007, 2008, 2010 and 2012, and again in 2015. Lost at Last Vol. 1 came out in 2017.
artist_reel_line: Lost at Last Vol. 1 came out in November 2017.

story: The Barr Brothers is a Montreal folk-blues band founded in 2006 by two American brothers, the drummer Andrew Barr and the guitarist Brad Barr. Their self-titled debut made the 2012 Polaris Music Prize long list, the year they played Pickathon, and Sleeping Operator, from October 2014, and Queens of the Breakers made later long lists. They returned to the farm in 2014, and their fourth studio album is Let It Hiss.

intro: A swing duo of upright bass and tenor guitar.
story: Andy Bean and Fuller Condon began as full-time buskers in New York's Central Park in 2005, Bean on banjo and tenor guitar and Condon on upright bass. Two at a Time, their sixth release, came out in 2012, and NPR's World Cafe Next featured it in May. They played Pickathon in 2007 and again that summer. In 2013 Bean became the composer for Disney's Wander Over Yonder, and the duo performs its theme song.
